main_text.p: Nonrequiri-tur hic alta profanarum literarum scientia.Hinc est quod literarum & humanæ sa-pientiæ versutiæque adminiculis usi, non-nullos sibi proseluthos lucrentur & magnatum animos concilient:quibus qui destituitur[?] ne se minus idcirco idoneum putet:si sacra Dei verba huc afferat sufficit, imò hæc tantum in hoc negocio valent. Unus enim hic gladius,spirituali adversario lethalis est: hæc fulgura ex throno Dei prodeuntia, cō-sumunt circumcirca adversarios ejus: si effœminatæ philosophiæ telis in aciemprodi-eris, risum ipsi potius quam metum move-bis; ab animali enim homine hujus militiæ arma fabricari nequeunt,sed hæc cum divi-nis(etiam ijs militibus quibus quædam talia suppetere videntur) commutanda sunt; ut omnia pro sordibus habetes,solum Chri-stum ejusque crucem, in simplicitate, potentia,& sapientia Spiritus Sancti sapiant; abjectaq;omni vafriciæ atque occultamento dedecoris, nomé ejus in synceritate præ-dicet. Quod fiet fælicissimè si versipelli veteris hominis naturâ depositâ, candorem agni Dei induerint: tunc orietur in tenebris lux eorum,& caligo illorum erit sicuti meridies:& erunt veluti hortus irriguus, velut scaturigo aquarum, cujus aquæ non defi-ciunt:exurgent ex ipsis qui ædificabunt deserta longi temporis, fundamenta genera-

page.notes: The first word of the page is not capitalised as a new paragraph, so the paragraph continues from the previous page. "destituitur" is read from "desti" at the line end with no printed hyphen; doubtful. The left margin note is printed in four short lines, joined here as one note. "nomé" and "cō" are printed with a tilde or accent as shown and are kept as they appear. The catchword "tionis" sits alone at the lower right and completes the hyphenated "generationis".
